grades.reason: Chapter exercises on race conditions and mutexes. The only related text is a pseudocode label saying 'in cache-conscious fashion', and it never explains why atomic-exchange spinlocks cause coherence traffic.
It covers nonblocking synchronization and compare-and-set. It says spinlocks use atomic exchange, but it says nothing about cache-coherence traffic or contention cost.

grades.quote: An example code sequence for a critical section guarded by a test-and-test-and-set spinlock is shown in Example Listing 3.
grades.reason: It gives a RISC-V test-and-test-and-set spinlock that spins on a plain load before attempting amoswap. That design implicitly addresses repeated atomic-exchange contention. It never explains the cache-line bouncing or coherence traffic, so it is only auxiliary.
It discusses the LR/SC atomicity axiom and the rarity of overlapping stores. It does not cover atomic-exchange spinlock contention or coherence traffic.
